claims.text: Certain high-value metallic components are susceptible to hot cracking during high-heat-input repair because of their microstructural characteristics.
A laser-cladding process can deposit a thin pre-alloyed powder layer onto a damaged metallic surface.
Controlled laser power and scan speed can provide rapid heating and cooling.
Controlled laser processing can minimize substrate dilution.
Controlled laser processing can restrict the heat-affected zone.
Laser cladding produces a refined, homogeneous, metallurgically bonded alloyed surface layer.
Laser cladding melts the pre-alloyed powder and a thin layer of the substrate.
Rapid resolidification after laser cladding creates a fine equiaxed microstructure.
The fine equiaxed microstructure enhances surface hardness.
The laser-clad microstructure increases resistance to hot cracking.
The laser-clad microstructure increases wear resistance.
The laser-clad microstructure increases corrosion resistance.
Laser-clad repairs will exhibit fewer hot-cracking incidents than both traditional fusion-welded repairs and untreated surfaces.
Laser-clad surfaces will have greater surface hardness than both traditional fusion-welded repairs and untreated surfaces.
Laser-clad surfaces will have greater wear resistance than both traditional fusion-welded repairs and untreated surfaces.
Laser-clad surfaces will have greater corrosion resistance than both traditional fusion-welded repairs and untreated surfaces.
Traditional fusion-welding repairs typically have wider heat-affected zones and greater hot-cracking susceptibility than laser-clad repairs.
Untreated surfaces typically have wider heat-affected zones and are more prone to hot cracking.
The effectiveness of laser cladding may vary substantially with substrate composition and service conditions.

contradictions.description: The baseline attributes a wider heat-affected zone to untreated surfaces, whereas the experiment treats them as an untreated control. A surface that has undergone no thermal repair does not acquire a repair-induced heat-affected zone.
